record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Dynamics of the Expression of Gene Interaction Networks
record.original_question: Assume each gene influences the expression of another gene through a nonlinear single-gene response rather than a linear additive term. In particular, for gene j affecting gene i, the contribution may be a Hill-type nonlinear function such as x_j^h / [1 + (x_j / x_{j0})^h] when gene j stimulates gene i, or 1 / [1 + (x_j / x_{j0})^h] when gene j inhibits gene i, where h is the Hill coefficient and x_{j0} is a constant. Given only experimentally observed attractor data x_f, and possibly limited intermediate observations x_n, what properties of the unknown nonlinear interaction rule A can be determined when A is a nonlinear function of the expression of each individual gene?

evidence.quote: 2) Open Problem II. Determine A where A is a Nonlinear Function of the Gene Expression of Each Gene.

Biochemical reactions are typically not linear functions and it is more likely that the contribution of each gene j to the expression of gene i is a nonlinear function. A typical such function is that the rate of expression of x_i is proportional to x_j^h/[1 + (x_j/x_j0)^h], where h is the Hill coefficient and x_j0 is a constant, if gene j stimulates gene i, or 1/[1 + (x_j/x_j0)^h] if gene j inhibits gene i.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a gene regulatory network with N genes whose expression levels at time t are given by x(t) = (x_1(t), ..., x_N(t)) ∈ R^N_{≥0}. Suppose the dynamics are governed by a system of the form

  dx_i/dt = F_i(x_1, ..., x_N) - γ_i x_i,   i = 1, ..., N,

where γ_i > 0 are degradation rates and the interaction term F_i is built from single-gene nonlinear responses; specifically, assume there exist sign labels s_{ij} ∈ {+1, -1, 0} (stimulation, inhibition, no interaction) and constants h > 0, x_{j0} > 0 such that

  F_i(x) = A_i( f_{i1}(x_1), f_{i2}(x_2), ..., f_{iN}(x_N) ),

where

  f_{ij}(x_j) = x_j^h / (1 + (x_j / x_{j0})^h)   if s_{ij} = +1,
  f_{ij}(x_j) = 1 / (1 + (x_j / x_{j0})^h)        if s_{ij} = -1,
  f_{ij}(x_j) = 0                                   if s_{ij} = 0,

and A_i : R^N → R is an unknown (possibly nonlinear) combining rule. Assume that the only experimental data available are:

(i) a finite collection {x_f^{(k)}}_{k=1}^K ⊂ R^N_{≥0} of observed attractors (equilibrium states) of the system, and
(ii) possibly a limited collection {x_n^{(ℓ)}}_{ℓ=1}^L of intermediate (non-equilibrium) observations of trajectories.

Problem. Determine which structural and quantitative properties of the unknown nonlinear interaction rule {A_i}_{i=1}^N — for instance, the sign pattern (s_{ij}), the Hill coefficient h, the thresholds x_{j0}, the functional form of A_i (additive, multiplicative, or other composition of the f_{ij}), and the identifiability of A_i up to equivalence — can be recovered from the data in (i) and (ii). In particular, give necessary and sufficient conditions on the attractor set, and on the size/nature of the intermediate observations, under which A is uniquely identifiable, and otherwise characterize the equivalence class of nonlinear rules A consistent with the data.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed explicitly as an open problem about identifying nonlinear (Hill-type) single-gene interaction rules from attractor data in gene regulatory network dynamics. No comprehensive resolution of identifiability for general nonlinear A from attractor data is reported; related work on inference of Hill-type GRNs continues to address only special or restricted cases.

status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly posed as an open problem about determining the nonlinear single-gene interaction rule A from attractor (and limited intermediate) data.
